text: Farrowing pen design is critical for piglet health and productivity. The sow must be able to stand up comfortably and drink freely (ad libitum). She should be contained in a farrowing cage to prevent her crushing piglets, especially in the days right after birth, while still allowing good access to the teats. Piglets must be protected from cold and drafts — a warm, sheltered 'nest' area is important during the night for the first 10 days of life, since cold piglets lose a lot of energy maintaining body temperature, become weak, and nurse less; cold on the abdomen also slows intestinal transit, which lets E. coli develop and triggers diarrhea. The floor should be kept dry to limit microbe growth; slatted floors work better than plain cement because urine and feces don't stay in contact with the piglets.
